## Current Engagements

SSCCS works with academia, industry, and open-hardware communities on problems where data movement, verification, or I/O dominates the cost. **Every engagement is judged by a demonstrable artifact: a fork, a benchmark, a measured report.** The table below lists the engagements in motion, the artifact each one delivers, and its status.

| Work | Institution | Artifact | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [CERN Collaboration Framework](cern/) | CERN | Framework draft for open-science engagement | Discussion |
| [ROOT TTree Bottleneck](cern/projects/root_ttree/) | CERN | Development plan and measured report | Plan draft, report published |
| [SSCCS Validation with OpenHW CORE-V Ecosystem](openhw_integration.html) | OpenHW Group | Phased integration roadmap | Proposal |
| [SSCCS × AWS Strategic Collaboration Roadmap](aws.html) | AWS | Phased collaboration proposal | Discussion |
| [A Foundation for Energy-Efficient and Trustworthy Computing](proposal.html) | Public | Funding and collaboration proposal | Published |
| [Presentation Deck](pt.pdf) | Public | Slide deck for outreach | Published |

The CERN engagement is the flagship work, and the reason is the mission. SSCCS is an independent, non-profit, public-good foundation that directs its technology toward the projects most aligned with the common good of humanity. CERN is the archetype of that alignment: a public-good science organization founded on the principle that science is a public good and knowledge remains open. The ROOT TTree bottleneck sits in the analysis framework of the entire high-energy physics community, and relieving it strengthens the open scientific infrastructure that researchers worldwide depend on. The collaboration framework establishes institutional alignment through CERN's open-source channels. The development plan specifies a bounded demonstration on CMS Open Data that reproduces the documented access pattern: 372,000 singular reads averaging 4.6 KB, an effective 33 KB/s, and a 14-hour workload. The report carries the measured comparison against the ROOT baseline. The ecosystem stays intact: researchers keep the TTree API they already know, and only the byte source changes.

## How a Collaboration Proceeds

Each engagement follows a bounded sequence, sized so the institution's production ecosystem is never disturbed.

- Alignment: a framework or proposal establishes the problem and the boundary.
- Bounded demonstration: a development plan specifies the artifact, the milestones, and the boundaries; the institution's stack runs unchanged.
- Measured result: a report compares against the institution's own baseline, on its own access pattern and data.
- Integration decision: the institution decides whether to adopt the result; the foundation's role ends at the boundary it defined.

## What SSCCS Brings

Every engagement is backed by a small set of validated primitives, all released under Apache 2.0:

- ExaVerif: exhaustive RISC-V verification, 33.5 million encodings in 29 ms.
- synTagma: hash-less coordinate addressing with a decoder of roughly 300 gates.
- Chton: zero-serialization storage; the storage format equals the memory layout, so the read path has no serialization step.

The codebases behind these primitives live under [Projects](/projects/).

## Engage with SSCCS

Engagements begin with a concrete problem. If your institution has a workload where data movement, verification, or I/O dominates the cost, the starting point is the [open proposal](proposal.html) or the [presentation deck](pt.pdf), and the direct route is a message to [proposal@ssccs.org](mailto:proposal@ssccs.org).

The foundation is independent and non-profit. Funding is a catalyst; engagements proceed on technical merit and reciprocal contribution, and all outputs remain open under Apache 2.0. The preference is research-first: institutions that fund research and development, provide demonstration environments, and value a measured artifact over a declared intention.
